findings.title: Capability board order and every Capability rank wiped in the v1.8.0 results
findings.evidence: data/raw/benchmarks/jevbench/v1.8/jevbench-v1.8.0-results.json: board.capability.order has 0 entries (v1.7.23: 283, all ranked rows sorted by capability desc); ranks.capability is null on all 314 rows (v1.7.23: 285 non-null). Cause: r198/v180/score_v180.mjs:13-17 loops over every key of a.board including 'capability' and sorts by s.scores[o]; scores has no 'capability' key, so the filter is empty and every ranks.capability is set to null. lib/jevbench-v180-release.mjs (the 'sorted composite board' loop over Object.keys(board)) checks the same wrong rule, so validator + tests pass. Built output: /api/jevbench/v1.8.0 serves the empty capability order and null ranks. Capability itself is unchanged, so these fields should be byte-equal to v1.7.23. The page's headline Capability ranking is not affected because it is computed by jevClassRows; consumers of ranks.capability (lib/jevbench-scope.mjs:77-86, lib/jevbench-cohort-merge.mjs:285-290, the public JSON) are.
findings.requested_change: In score_v180.mjs recompute only A/B/C (skip 'capability'), or rebuild capability exactly like v1.7.23 (ranked rows by capability desc, the same tie rule). Keep the 2 unranked rows' carried capability ranks (apus-openjev-v1-35b-a3b 66, bb-qwen3.5-4b-lora 65) as they were. Fix the validator loop in lib/jevbench-v180-release.mjs to A/B/C plus an explicit capability equality with v1.7.23. Re-pin the exceptions.

findings.title: Conflict of interest the GO card must disclose: the new open Capability #1 is mammoth-1, which Decision Models sells as s1-pro-5
findings.evidence: Open headline Capability before: h2o-lightning-31b, basal-omni-1.0-ultra, dopest-1.0-31b, jeff_1_1_medium, arcbright-elf-1-31b; after: mammoth-1 (85.233), knowline-31b-gen1 (85.213), fastino-glide-1.2-open, h2o-lightning-31b, pplx-decider-v1-1-27b. DECISIONS.md line 145: 'The new open #1 (mammoth-1 = our s1-pro-5)'. mammoth-1 enters only because the method changed (v1.7: USD 0.1036 = 1.60x the cap; v1.8: USD 0.0268, D5 base-arch measurement with the block-bidirectional attention left out). The page only has the general 'Decision Models is run by the same company' line under 'Use'. No row-level disclosure. The new open #1 and #2 differ by 0.02 Capability points.

findings.title: Top-five entries that rest on substitute-trunk or thin-margin estimates
findings.evidence: fastino-glide-1.2-open (open #3, A #5) and pplx-decider-v1-1-27b (open #5) use 'trunk-equivalent' D5 throughput: the stock Qwen3.8-27B trunk, not their own weights or readout. mammoth-1 uses base-arch. knowline-31b-gen1 (open #2) is eligible at 0.94x the cap (USD 0.0608 vs 0.0646): a 6 % margin that depends on the 70 % load assumption (the class value would give 0.956x). All token counts in the top five were verified: I recomputed them from published totals or raw run sums. None rests on an unverified token count.
findings.requested_change: Name these in the GO card (estimate basis + margin). No data change needed.

findings.title: Same rule, different treatment: diffusion rows and non-Gemma/Qwen small decoders
findings.evidence: Three DiffusionGemma rows (diffusion-jev: '48-step diffusion readout'; openjev-thinking: 365 generated tokens per decision; open-jev-json-canvas-joshuasp) are priced with the autoregressive MoE-Gemma prefill constant. nemotron-diffusion-8b is excluded as 'unresolvable'. Seven rows with verified usage (standard_one_3b_sh/_v4/_8b_sh and standardone-8b on Ministral-3, pjev-2b/jul-fast/decision-2b/smalljev on MiniCPM5, exaone-4.0-1.2b, liquid-d1-3b) keep their old cost. The reference model (model/out/rows.csv) restated several of them as small-Qwen proxies, e.g. standard_one_8b_sh 0.0782 -> 0.0102. Public text calls them 'unresolved architectures', but they are known dense decoders outside the six calibrated families. More generally, generated output tokens are charged at prefill throughput (calibration max_tokens=1). The text says 'scored inputs and outputs' but does not say throughput is prefill-only. None of these rows is near the top five.
findings.requested_change: Lead/Florian decision: either exclude diffusion rows like nemotron, or disclose them. Reword 'unresolved architectures' to 'architectures outside the six calibrated Gemma/Qwen classes'. Add one sentence that throughput was measured as prefill and that generated tokens are counted at that rate.

findings.title: Minor presentation notes
findings.evidence: The board eyebrow still reads 'Method v1.7 (10 s rule)' on v1.8.0. In dense Qwen the constant 317,601 is 27 x the rounded 11,763; the unrounded measurement gives 317,597 (1.3e-5 relative). That is spec-conformant. The per-row composite_interval_note is not rendered; the withheld CIs show as '—' and are disclosed in the methodology section, the release note and the page header text.
